name: Armando al Pantheon
blurb: Family-run trattoria a few steps from the Pantheon.
guide: The Gargioli family has served Roman classics here since 1961: fettuccine with chicken innards, slow-cooked tripe, braised artichokes, and puntarelle with anchovy dressing.

name: Cesare al Pellegrino
blurb: Centro sibling of Cesare al Casaletto, between Campo de' Fiori and Via Giulia.

name: Cesare al Casaletto
blurb: Neighborhood trattoria at the end of the 8 tram line, known for fritti and pasta.
guide: New ownership brought refined technique while keeping the neighborhood spirit: food that feels traditional, executed with more precision.

name: Osteria Bonelli
blurb: Busy, inexpensive neighborhood osteria with a daily chalkboard menu.

name: Tavernaccia da Bruno
address: Via Giovanni da Castel Bolognese 63, Roma
blurb: Family trattoria with Roman and Umbrian dishes and roasts from the wood oven.

name: Piatto Romano
blurb: Testaccio trattoria for Roman classics and heirloom local vegetables.

name: Hosteria Grappolo d'Oro
blurb: Roman pastas, meatballs and seasonal sides near Campo de' Fiori.

name: Trecca
blurb: 'Cucina di mercato' trattoria with a focus on quinto quarto and Roman classics.

name: Ai Marmi
blurb: Also called Panattoni: marble tables, ultra-thin Roman pizza, supplì and baccalà.

name: A Rota
blurb: 'Pizzeria romanesca' for crisp, thin Roman pizza and fritti.

name: La Gatta Mangiona
blurb: Long-running Monteverde pizzeria with creative monthly pies and deep wine and beer lists.

name: L'Elementare
blurb: Thin, crisp 'scrocchiarella' Roman pizza and creative supplì.

name: L'Elementare
blurb: Two-floor branch just across Ponte Testaccio.

name: L'Elementare
blurb: Tuscolano branch of the thin-crust pizza group.

name: L'Elementare
blurb: San Giovanni outpost; mainly takeaway and delivery.

name: L'Elementare
address: Piazza di Santa Maria Consolatrice 1, Roma
blurb: Newest branch, opened September 2026.

name: I Quintili
blurb: Contemporary Neapolitan-style pizza with Roman touches.

name: I Quintili
blurb: Larger branch with plenty of outdoor seating.

name: Piccolo Buco
blurb: Tiny pizzeria near the Trevi Fountain known for airy crusts and top Italian ingredients.

name: VICO Pizza & Wine
blurb: Neapolitan pizza and a serious wine list, near the Pantheon.

name: Frumentario
blurb: Pizza in teglia with toppings finished at the counter.

name: Lievito
blurb: Francesco Arnesano's sourdough teglia, breads and supplì.

name: Nonnarè
blurb: Neighborhood slice shop for thin, crisp Roman teglia.

name: Pizzarium
blurb: Gabriele Bonci's slice shop near the Cipro metro stop.
guide: The guide credits Bonci with elevating pizza in teglia: long-fermented doughs from stone-milled grains, topped with highly seasonal ingredients.

name: Pantera
blurb: Tiny slice shop from the Trecca team, prized for a thin, crunchy base.

name: Ruver Teglia Frazionata
blurb: Small shop selling pre-portioned teglia by the piece.

name: Amerina
blurb: Small pan-baked pizzette, steps from Campo de' Fiori.

name: Mordi e Vai
blurb: Box 15 in the Testaccio Market: panini filled with Roman braises and offal.
guide: Founded by butcher Sergio Esposito and now run by his son. Ciabatta is filled with braised meats and traditional Roman recipes originally developed for family meals.

name: C'è Pasta e Pasta
blurb: Kosher fresh-pasta shop and canteen for Roman-Jewish dishes, near Trastevere station.

name: Trapizzino
blurb: The original shop: pizza pockets stuffed with Roman stews, plus supplì.

name: Trapizzino
blurb: Sit-down Trapizzino with a wine list, by Ponte Sisto.

name: Trapizzino
blurb: Trapizzini and supplì with sidewalk seating, open late.

name: Trapizzino
blurb: Counter inside the Be.Re. craft-beer bar, near the Vatican.

name: Trapizzino
blurb: Stall in the Mercato Centrale food hall at Termini.

name: Da Corrado
blurb: Box 18 in the Testaccio Market: a few stools, regional dishes and natural wine.

name: Supplizio
blurb: Supplì and other Roman fried snacks.

name: Becco
blurb: Takeaway tramezzini with house pickles and ferments.

name: Andreotti
blurb: Historic family pastry shop: maritozzi, crostate and holiday sweets.

name: Barnum
blurb: Specialty coffee, laminated pastries and brunch. Moved to this address in 2026.

name: Casa Manfredi Teatro
blurb: Pastry lab and café in a former theatre: croissants, maritozzi, cakes.

name: Gastromario
blurb: Pastries and viennoiserie plus fresh pasta and bistro cooking.

name: Gruè
blurb: Modern pastry shop: cakes, mignon, lievitati and gelato.

name: Slow
blurb: Specialty coffee and pastry lab near Largo Argentina.

name: Luna
blurb: Specialty café-bakery from the Faro team, uphill from Piazza Barberini.

name: Nero Vaniglia
blurb: Neighborhood pastry shop for breakfast pastries, cakes and gelato.

name: Roscioli Caffè
blurb: The Roscioli family's café: maritozzi, cornetti and espresso.

name: SAID dal 1923
blurb: Historic chocolate factory with a shop, café and bistro.

name: Boccione
blurb: Historic kosher bakery: pizza ebraica and ricotta and sour-cherry tart.

name: Al Settimo Gelo
blurb: Natural gelato, strong on seasonal fruit and unusual flavors.

name: Fatamorgana
blurb: Gluten-free artisan gelato with inventive flavors.

name: Fatamorgana
blurb: Gluten-free artisan gelato on a quiet Monti piazza.

name: Fatamorgana
blurb: Gluten-free artisan gelato near Piazza San Cosimato.

name: Fior di Luna
blurb: Small natural gelateria using organic and fair-trade ingredients.

name: Formaessenza
blurb: Design-minded gelato served in jars, on sticks and as bonbons.

name: Gelateria dei Gracchi
blurb: The original shop, known for seasonal fruit flavors.

name: Gelateria dei Gracchi
blurb: Central branch near Piazza del Popolo.

name: Gelateria dei Gracchi
blurb: Nomentano branch.

name: Gelateria del Teatro
blurb: Visible lab; herb flavors like sage and raspberry.

name: Gelateria Gori
blurb: Montesacro gelateria for natural, creative flavors and semifreddi.

name: La Gourmandise
blurb: Neighborhood gelateria with pure, balanced natural flavors.

name: Neve di Latte
blurb: Natural gelato made with organic milk.

name: Neve di Latte
blurb: The original shop, near MAXXI.

name: Neve di Latte
blurb: Branch by Piazza Cavour.

name: Otaleg!
blurb: Gelato with a visible lab, classic and creative flavors.

name: Otaleg!
blurb: Larger shop with gelato lab, pastry and café.

name: Torcè
blurb: Claudio Torcè's natural gelato, including savory flavors.
guide: The guide calls Claudio Torcè one of modern Roman gelato's most important figures: he trained many of the city's top gelato makers and is known for more than 100 all-natural flavors.

name: Torcè
blurb: EUR shop of the natural-gelato pioneer.

name: Mercato di Campagna Amica del Circo Massimo
blurb: Producers from around Lazio selling direct. Weekends, mornings to mid-afternoon.

name: Mercato di San Giovanni di Dio
address: Piazza San Giovanni di Dio, Roma
blurb: Big, affordable Monteverde market for produce and fish. Mornings, Monday to Saturday.

name: Mercato Trionfale
blurb: Huge covered market near the Vatican. Mornings, Monday to Saturday.

name: Nuovo Mercato di Testaccio
blurb: Covered market mixing produce and butcher stalls with street-food counters.
guide: Home to the Mordi e Vai stall, which is now in its second generation.

name: Mercato Campo Marzio
blurb: Tiny covered neighborhood market, about a dozen stalls, near Piazza Borghese.

name: Nuovo Mercato Esquilino
blurb: Multicultural covered market: spices, halal meat and produce from around the world.

name: Forme Dispensa a Ripa
address: Via di San Francesco a Ripa 71, Roma
blurb: Artisan cheeses, salumi, anchovies and natural wine.

name: La Differenza
blurb: Family pizzicheria for salumi, cheese and wine, now with a bistrot.

name: La Formaggeria
blurb: Cheese stall (boxes 25–26) inside Mercato Latino, with cheeses from small producers.

name: Panificio Fiore
blurb: Bari Vecchia bakery famous for focaccia baked in oil-drenched iron pans: crisp underneath, spongy inside.
order: The focaccia topped with tomatoes and olives (watch for pits).

name: Di Cosimo
blurb: A Bari landmark for pizza and panzerotti, pizza dough stuffed with mozzarella and tomato and deep-fried.
order: Queue for takeout, or look for a table in the side room.

name: Da Tuccino
address: Contrada Santa Caterina 69/F, 70044 Polignano a Mare
blurb: Upscale seafood restaurant on the sea, with some of the best pesce crudo in the province.
order: The crudi, octopus salad and spaghetti con le cozze.
warn: Pin is approximate (the address is a rural contrada); the Directions link finds the restaurant.

name: Super Mago del Gelo
address: Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi 22, 70044 Polignano a Mare
blurb: Granita specialist; each portion comes with two flavors.
order: Gelso nero (black mulberry) and mandorla (almond). Pay at the register first, and add panna if you want it.

name: Lido Bianco
blurb: Seafront restaurant by Porto Bianco beach, recommended for more crudi.

name: La Rotonda
blurb: No-frills shack with a patio over the water on the coast road between Savelletri and Torre Canne.
order: Sea urchins in season, served with bread to scoop the roe, plus grilled octopus and cozze fritte.
warn: Also listed as La Rotonda (Da Rosa); don't confuse it with La Rotonda 2 in Torre Canne village.

name: L'Aratro
blurb: An alternative to Alberobello's tourist traps, run by a sommelier who cooks with Slow Food products.
order: Orecchiette con cime di rapa, fave e cicoria, capocollo and local cheeses.

name: La Succursale
blurb: One of the few Lecce restaurants where she says you'll eat well.

name: Quanto Basta
blurb: Mixes some of the best cocktails in southern Italy.

name: Caffè Alvino
blurb: Bar and caffè on the main piazza, and her first stop in Lecce every time.
order: A rustico (puff pastry with béchamel, mozzarella, tomato and black pepper) and a pasticciotto, eaten standing at the bar.

name: Pasticceria Citiso
blurb: Pastry shop she recommends for pasticciotti, cream-filled shortcrust tarts.

name: Gelateria Natale
blurb: Gelateria and pastry shop off Piazza Sant'Oronzo, known for flavors based on local sweets.
order: Gelato al pasticciotto and gelato al mustazzolo.

name: Avio
blurb: Coffee bar near the Castello pouring a special blend of local Quarta coffee.
order: The espressino freddo: whipped cream, espresso, cremino and caramel in a goblet.
warn: Closed for a refit in late 2024; check it has reopened before you go.

name: Le Zie
blurb: Home-style cooking with views into the kitchen.
order: The antipasto misto, fave e cicoria and pezzetti di cavallo.
warn: Her more recent post says it was a letdown on her last visit.

name: Pasticceria Nobile
blurb: Hole-in-the-wall on the sea that she calls the best pasticciotti in the region, turned out hot all day.

name: L'Orecchietta
blurb: Family-run trattoria, once a pasta shop, serving traditional food cafeteria style with an excellent local wine list.
warn: Open at lunch, closed in the afternoon, then open again until 8 PM.

name: Caffè Parisi
blurb: Bar on the main square with a great spirits selection and a pretty patio for aperitivo or an after-dinner drink.

name: Peccato di Vino
blurb: Her pick if you have to eat in Otranto, which she otherwise calls full of tourist traps.

name: Farmacia dei Sani
blurb: Very good cooking, though a bit fancier than typical Salento fare.

name: Rua de Li Travaj
blurb: Where to go for traditional Salento dishes.

name: Bleu Salento
blurb: A reliable option if you're eating in Gallipoli, at the Bleu Salento marina.

name: Le Macàre
blurb: Her pick for properly good food near Gallipoli, 20 minutes inland.
